note: Kept existing draft. Molina 1571 'ocelotl: tigre'; Karttunen 1983 ocēlōtl. Also a day sign of the tonalpohualli, but the everyday animal noun; not a deity name.
Kept existing draft. Molina 'huitzitzilin: pájaro pequeño de pluma rica'; Karttunen huitzitzilin. Root of the deity name Huitzilopochtli, but the bird noun itself is ordinary.

review_question: ¿Se dice "llama" tal cual en náhuatl, o hay otra palabra que usen para este animal?
note: Spanish word, not traditional Nahuatl. Llamas are Andean; no native referent. ichcatl (cotton; post-contact "sheep") would mislead.

review_question: ¿Cómo se dice "cóndor" en su variante: se usa la palabra española, o se diría algo como "huey tzopilotl"?
note: Spanish word, not traditional Nahuatl. The Andean condor has no Classical name. A descriptive phrase huey tzopilotl (huey "great" + tzopilotl "vulture", Molina s.v. tzopilotl) was considered but would be coined for this deck, not traditional, so it is offered only as an alternative. cozcacuauhtli (king vulture) is a different bird and a day sign; avoided.
Molina 'papalotl: mariposa'; Karttunen pāpālōtl. Widely kept in modern varieties (papalotl/papalot). Source of Mexican Spanish papalote (kite). papalotl sounds close to papa; avoidWith set.
Molina 'huexolotl: gallo de la tierra'; source of Spanish guajolote. totolin is the generic/hen term and an alternative; the card shows a displaying male, so huexolotl fits.
Molina 'ayotl: tortuga'; Karttunen āyōtl. RISK: without length marks it looks like ayohtli/ayotli 'squash'; reviewer may want a disambiguating spelling or diacritics.
Molina 'cueyatl: rana'; Karttunen cuēyatl. Modern forms vary (kueyatl, kuiyatl).
Molina 'coatl: culebra'; Karttunen cōātl. Ordinary noun; it is part of Quetzalcoatl and a day sign, but standing alone it is just 'snake'.
Kept existing draft. Molina 'centli: maçorca de maíz seca'. Alternatives: tlaolli (shelled kernels), elotl (green ear), cintli (variant spelling). Root of Centeotl, but the noun itself is everyday.
Kept existing draft. Molina 'nopalli: tunal, árbol'. Source of Spanish nopal. Fruit is nochtli (tuna).
Kept existing draft. Molina 'etl: frisol'; Karttunen ētl. Very short for a caller; reviewer may prefer a modern form (e.g. et, yetl in some varieties).

review_question: ¿Cómo se dice "piña" en su variante? ¿Conoce la palabra "matzatli" para la piña?
note: Spanish word, not traditional Nahuatl. I have a recollection of "matzatli" being given for pineapple, but I cannot name a dictionary or page for it, so it is unverified and not used.
Kept existing draft. Molina 'chilli: axí'; Karttunen chīlli.

review_question: ¿Se dice "papa" en náhuatl en su comunidad, o hay una palabra propia para la papa (no el camote)?
note: Spanish word, not traditional Nahuatl. Potato is Andean and post-contact in Mexico. Do NOT use camohtli (sweet potato, camote).
Kept existing draft. Molina 'ahuacatl: fruta que llaman aguacate'; Karttunen āhuacatl. Note: also slang for testicle in Classical sources; harmless here but reviewer should be aware.

CHANGED from existing draft tomatl. In central Mexico tomatl is mainly the green husk tomato (tomatillo); the red tomato on this card ('rojo y jugoso') is xitomatl (Molina/Karttunen; source of Mexican Spanish jitomate). If the reviewer wants the generic term, revert to tomatl.

review_question: ¿Cómo se dice "girasol" en su variante: chimalxochitl, chimalacatl u otra?
note: chimalli "shield" + xochitl "flower". Commonly cited for sunflower in early colonial botanical sources (Hernández); chimalacatl "shield reed" is another cited form. I have not checked the primary entry myself. Fallback: loanword "girasol".

gloss: sun (lit. 'one who goes along giving warmth/light')
review_question: "Tonatiuh" también es nombre de una deidad. ¿Le parece bien usarlo como la palabra común para "sol" en un juego para niños, o prefiere otra (tonati, tonaltzin…)?
note: Kept existing draft. Molina 'tonatiuh: el sol' is the ordinary Classical noun for the sun. CAUTION: identical to the deity name Tonatiuh. No separate profane noun exists in Classical; tonalli means sun's heat/day but also 'soul, day sign' (more ritual-loaded). Modern varieties use tonati, tonaltzin, etc. Reviewer must decide whether this is acceptable for the card.
Kept existing draft. Molina 'metztli: luna o mes'. Also the name of a lunar deity in some sources, but primarily the ordinary noun. Sounds close to mixtli (nube); avoidWith set.
Molina 'citlalin: estrella'; Karttunen citlalin. Modern forms: sitlalin, sitlali.
Molina 'quiahuitl: lluvia'; Karttunen quiyahuitl (also spelled quiyahuitl). Also a day sign; ordinary noun.

review_question: ¿Cómo se dice "rayo" o "relámpago" en su variante?
note: petlani "to flash, shine" with tla- and the -lli patient nominal: tlapetlanilli "something flashed". I believe Molina has related forms (tlapetlaniliztli) for relámpago but I have not verified this exact form. Coined for this deck, not traditional.

gloss: rainbow (ayahuitl "mist" + cozamalotl; literal sense of the second element uncertain)
review_question: ¿Cómo se dice "arcoíris" en su variante? ¿Se usa "ayauhcozamalotl" o una forma más corta?
note: Molina 'ayauhcoçamalotl: arco del cielo'; ayahuitl 'mist' + cozamalotl. Long for a caller; modern varieties often shorten or use other forms. Literal gloss of cozamalotl is debated.
Molina 'mixtli: nube'; Karttunen mixtli.

review_question: "Ehecatl" también es nombre de una deidad. ¿Le parece bien como palabra común para "viento" en un juego para niños, o prefiere otra forma?
note: Molina 'ehecatl: viento'; Karttunen ehēcatl. CAUTION: same form as the wind deity Ehecatl and a day sign; it is the ordinary noun but reviewer should judge, as with tonatiuh. Modern forms: ejekatl, ajakatl.

review_question: ¿Cómo se dice "cometa" (estrella con cola) en su variante? ¿Se usa "citlalin popoca"?
note: citlalin "star" + popoca "it smokes": a clause, "the star smokes". I recall Molina giving this for cometa but cannot confirm the entry, so treated as descriptive. Until verified, treat as coined for this deck, not traditional. Shares citlalin with estrella, so the two must not be offered together.
Kept existing draft. Molina 'tepetl: monte o sierra'. Shares tepetl with volcan and pueblo (altepetl); avoidWith set.

review_question: ¿Hay una palabra general para "volcán" en su variante? ¿Se entiende "popocani tepetl" o suena raro?
note: popoca "to smoke" (intransitive verb) + -ni (customary agentive on present stem) gives popocani "one that smokes", used here as a modifier before tepetl "mountain". Classical would more naturally compound verb stem + noun as popocatepetl, but that is the proper name of one volcano, so avoided. Coined for this deck, not traditional.
Molina 'ameyalli: fuente o manantial'; from atl 'water' + meya 'to flow'.

review_question: ¿Cómo se dice "mar" en su variante: ilhuicaatl, hueyatl, "mar" u otra?
note: Molina 'ilhuicaatl: la mar'; ilhuicatl 'sky' + atl 'water'. Alternatives: hueyatl ('great water'), teoatl (has teo- 'divine' element, avoided). Modern speakers may just say hueyatl or loan 'mar'.

review_question: ¿Cómo se dice "desierto" (tierra seca con poca lluvia) en su variante?
note: huaqui "to dry out" (preterit agentive huacqui "dried") + tlalli "land": "dried-up land". Coined for this deck, not traditional. Attested ixtlahuatl means open plain/savanna, not quite desert.

review_question: ¿Cuauhtla sirve para "selva" (bosque tropical con mucha lluvia) o solo para "bosque"?
note: Molina 'quauhtla: arboleda o montaña de árboles'; cuahuitl 'tree' + -tla (abundance). Means forest generally, not specifically tropical jungle. Modern varieties: kuoujtla, kuatitla.

review_question: ¿Conoce "tehuilotl" para el cristal de roca? ¿Cómo lo dicen?
note: Molina 'tehuilotl: cristal'; Sahagún Book 11 describes it among stones. Confident in the word, less in spelling (te- 'stone' + huilotl?).

review_question: ¿Cómo se dice "isla" (tierra rodeada de agua) en náhuatl en su variante?
note: Spanish word, not traditional Nahuatl. Replaced the earlier draft anepantla tlalli, which reviewer judged ungrammatical (adverbial anepantla juxtaposed to a noun without a proper construction). I know no reliable single Classical noun for island.
Molina 'oztotl: cueva'; Karttunen oztōtl. Caves have ritual significance in Mesoamerica but the noun is ordinary.
Molina 'comitl: olla'; Karttunen comitl. Related comalli (griddle).
Molina 'chiquihuitl: cesto o canasta'; source of Mexican Spanish chiquihuite. Alternative petlacalli is a lidded reed box, not a basket.

Molina 'huehuetl: atabal'. The drum used in ceremonial dance, but the instrument noun is ordinary. Alternative teponaztli is the slit drum. Homophone in unmarked spelling with huehue 'old man' is a mild risk.

review_question: ¿Cómo se dice "adobe" (ladrillo de barro y paja) en su variante? ¿Se usa "xamitl"?
note: Molina 'xamitl: adobe'. I am fairly but not fully sure of this entry; check against Molina directly.
Molina 'icpatl: hilo'; Karttunen icpatl.
Molina 'acalli: barca, navío o canoa'; atl 'water' + calli 'house'.

review_question: ¿Cómo se dice "puente" en su variante? ¿Se usa "cuauhpantli" también para puentes que no son de madera?
note: Molina 'quauhpantli: puente de madera'; cuahuitl 'wood' + pantli 'row, flag'. Strictly a wooden footbridge; a modern road bridge may be called by loan 'puente'.

review_question: ¿Cómo se dice "vela" (de cera) en su variante?
note: xicocuitlatl "beeswax" + ocotl "pine torch": "wax torch". Coined for this deck, not traditional. I believe a similar form may occur in colonial texts but cannot cite it. Colonial Nahuatl also borrowed "candela"; modern speakers often say "vela".

review_question: ¿Cómo se dice "martillo" en su variante: "martillo" o una palabra náhuatl?
note: tla- + tzotzona "to beat, hammer" + -loni (instrumental): "thing for pounding". Coined for this deck, not traditional. tzotzona also means to play a drum, so it clashes with tambor. Alternatives: tepoztlatzotzonaloni (metal pounder), loanword "martillo".
Molina 'calli: casa'. Also a day sign; ordinary noun. Modern: kali, kalli.
Molina 'milli: heredad'; Spanish milpa from milpan 'in the field'. Modern speakers may use milpa itself.

review_question: ¿Cómo se dice "tienda" (la de la esquina) en su variante?
note: tla- + namaca "to sell" + -oyan "place": "place where things are sold". Regular morphology, but not verified as attested or in use. Coined for this deck, not traditional. Alternative: loanword "tienda".

review_question: Para la plaza del centro del pueblo (no el mercado), ¿qué palabra usan: tianquiztli, ithualli, "plaza" u otra?
note: tianquiztli is a market, not a town square; the card shows a square with a fountain and benches, so the meaning does not fit well. Alternatives: ithualli (courtyard, patio), loanword "plaza".

gloss: place where canoes are laid up/moored
review_question: ¿Cómo se dice "puerto" (donde llegan y se amarran las barcas) en su variante?
note: acalli "canoe" + teca "to lay down" + -oyan "place": "place where canoes are laid up". I suspected a similar Molina entry but cannot confirm. Coined for this deck, not traditional. Alternative: loanword "puerto".
Molina 'altepetl: pueblo'; atl 'water' + tepetl 'mountain'. Historically a city-state/polity; for a small village calpolli (neighbourhood) is an alternative. Widely used today for 'pueblo'.

review_question: ¿Cómo se dice "escuela" en su variante: tlamachtiloyan, tlamachtilcalli, "escuela" u otra?
note: tla- + machtia "to teach" + -lo- (impersonal) + -yan "place": "place where people are taught". I believe forms like this are used in bilingual education but cannot cite a source, so not labelled neologism. Coined for this deck, not traditional. Avoided calmecac/telpochcalli (pre-contact institutions with ritual roles).

gloss: place where one looks at the stars
review_question: ¿Cómo se diría "observatorio" (lugar para mirar las estrellas) en su variante?
note: citlal(in) "star" + tlachia "to look" + -lo- + -yan "place": "place where stars are looked at"; compare tlachialoni "lookout". Coined for this deck, not traditional. Long; loanword "observatorio" is an alternative.

review_question: ¿Cómo se dice "biblioteca" en su variante? ¿Se entiende "amoxcalli"?
note: amoxtli "book, codex" + calli "house": "book house". Transparent compound; I cannot cite traditional or institutional use for "library". Coined for this deck, not traditional. Alternative: amoxpialoyan "place where books are kept".
